name: ice_core
title: Ice Core - iCE40UP5K FPGA + RP2040 dev board, 6 layers
brief: FPGA + MCU dev board on 6 layers: a Lattice iCE40UP5K-SG48 booting from a W25Q32 SPI flash, with an 8 MB APS6404L QSPI PSRAM on its user I/O, three 12-pin Pmod host ports and its dedicated RGB LED driver on a common-anode RGB LED; an RP2040 with its own QSPI flash and 12 MHz crystal acts as the USB bridge and FPGA programmer (it drives CRESET_B, reads CDONE, shares the configuration SPI and clocks the FPGA from GPOUT0). USB-C with USBLC6 ESD; an AP63203 buck makes 3.3 V and an AP2112K-1.2 LDO the 1.2 V core with the iCE40 VCCPLL filter; BOOT, RESET and USER buttons, PWR / ACT / DONE LEDs, four M3 holes.

blocks.title: RP2040: USB bridge and FPGA programmer
RGB LED on the iCE40 RGB driver

netClasses.name: VIN
netClasses.why: USB input current; every VBUS pad (receptacle, USBLC6, buck, LDO) takes 0.4 mm

netClasses.name: RAIL
netClasses.why: 3V3 has 54 pins and must be routed as tracks before any pour; 0.2 mm (IPC-2221 at 10 C rise: 0.74 A on 1 oz outer copper, 0.23 A on 0.5 oz inner, route.ipc2221_amps) leaves room for the signals, and In3 becomes a solid 3V3 plane once routing reaches 0 open. The 1.2 V core draws tens of mA

rules.why_clearance: the RP2040's QFN-56 has 0.2 mm pads at 0.4 mm pitch: 0.15 mm track and clearance enter a pad without touching its neighbours; JLCPCB's multilayer line builds 0.09 mm. 0.127 mm was measured and refused: the pipeline's hole clearance stays 0.25 mm, and the run gave 123 hole_clearance and 6 track_width DRC rows
rules.why_min_track: Freerouting may neck a track to 0.10 mm into a fine-pitch pad; JLCPCB's multilayer line builds 0.09 mm

board.notes: 6 layers: F.Cu signal / In1 GND plane / In2 signal / In3 power plane (the dominant rail, 'auto') / In4 GND plane / B.Cu signal. Planes are Specctra power layers while routing, so Freerouting routes on F.Cu, In2 and B.Cu; every plane is poured only after routing measures 0 open.

usb:J?.why: plug enters from the top edge, shell 0.6 mm proud

pmod_a:J?.why: Pmod A opens on the top edge, facing the FPGA's top-side pins

pmod_c:J?.why: Pmod C opens on the right edge, facing the FPGA's right-side pins

pmod_b:J?.why: Pmod B opens on the bottom edge, facing the FPGA's bottom-side pins

fpga:U?.why: FPGA in the middle of its three Pmod ports

fpga:C6?.why: 3V3 100 nF on the bottom-left corner diagonal, clear of the left-side escape

fpga:C2?.why: VCC (pin 5) 100 nF on the top-left corner diagonal

fpga:C3?.why: VCC (pin 30) 100 nF on the top-right corner diagonal

fpga:C1?.why: 1.2 V bulk 4.7 uF beside the LDO, off the FPGA's escape channels; the 100 nF caps stay at the pins

fpga:C10?.why: 3.3 V bank bulk 4.7 uF beside the buck output; In3 carries 3V3 to the FPGA after routing

fpga:C11?.why: second 3.3 V bank bulk 4.7 uF beside the buck output

fpga:R2?.why: CRESET_B pull-up by the RP2040 GPIO20 that drives it, not in the FPGA's escape

fpga:R3?.why: CDONE pull-up by the RP2040 GPIO22 that reads it

fpga:R4?.why: SPI_SS_B pull-up under the configuration flash

fpga:R5?.why: SPI_SCK pull-up under the configuration flash

mcu:U?.why: RP2040 under the USB-C, its SPI0 corner toward the FPGA

bflash:U?.why: boot flash at the RP2040's top-left corner, where its QSPI pins are

psram:U?.why: PSRAM between the chips, beside the FPGA's left-side pins

cflash:U?.why: configuration flash between the RP2040's SPI0 pins and the FPGA's SPI pins

buck:U?.why: buck between the USB-C and Pmod A, close to VBUS

core:U?.why: 1.2 V LDO above the FPGA's left side

esd:U?.why: ESD clamp right under the receptacle

rgb:D?.why: RGB LED near the FPGA's RGB pins, clear of the Pmods

led_pwr:R?.why: status LEDs in a column on the left edge

led_act:R?.why: status LEDs in a column on the left edge

led_done:R?.why: status LEDs in a column on the left edge

fpga:C8?.why: VPP_2V5 100 nF on the bottom-right corner diagonal

fpga:C4?.why: VCCPLL 4.7 uF below-right of the FPGA, out of Pmod C's escape; the 100 nF stays at pin 29 (a satellite)

fpga:R1?.why: VCCPLL 100 ohm beside its 4.7 uF, out of Pmod C's escape

route.why_via_in_pad: the iCE40's 5.6 mm and the RP2040's 3.2 mm exposed pads are walled in by 0.5 / 0.4 mm-pitch pins: no 0.15 mm track fits between two pins, so ground reaches them only through a via in the pad (the first run left U6.49 open on every rung)
route.why: the ladder is computed from each rung's opens: narrow the classes that carry an open net to 0.2 mm; the outline is stated, so it is never grown

captions.place_3d: KiCad's raytracer on the placed board: USB-C and Pmod A on the top edge, Pmod C on the right, Pmod B on the bottom, the RP2040 left and the iCE40UP5K centre-right.
